answer: The onyx of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The atlas is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the vertex. Written in a verbs first, step by step register, it stays short. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, split across independent auditors, idle agents bleed standing. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce.
